title: the HEVC reference-set fill writes up to eight bytes past an eight-entry array into the next array of the same struct
live_proof: LIVE: the fix's three-way FF_ARRAY_ELEMS guard is absent from n9.0.1:libavcodec/vulkan_hevc.c, which runs straight from the nb_refs loop at :766-767 into 'memset(hp->h265pic.RefPicSetStCurrBefore, 0xff, 8);' at :768 and the unguarded 'hp->h265pic.RefPicSetStCurrBefore[i] = j;' at :775. The array width of 8 is proved by the pin's own memset; the loop bound comes from a RefPicList holding up to HEVC_MAX_REFS = 16 (n9.0.1:libavcodec/hevc/hevc.h:120-122).
object: HEVCVulkanDecodePicture, one refstruct allocation (decode.c:2352 with frame_priv_data_size = sizeof(HEVCVulkanDecodePicture))
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Sub-object spatial row.
shape: array member written past its end into the next array of the same allocation
allocator_layer: av_refstruct over av_malloc: one allocation for the whole picture-private struct
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. Reduced to the three reference-set arrays and a following field, at the real declared width of 8, with the loop bound at the real HEVC_MAX_REFS of 16. Vulkan itself is not needed to reproduce the index arithmetic.
distinguishing: the most tightly contained row: the spill is exactly 8 bytes into an 8-byte neighbour, so there is NO magnitude at which it leaves the allocation. The case asserts the field after the three arrays is untouched.
note: upstream reachability is Vulkan-hwaccel builds only, and nb_refs > 8 is asserted by the fix's own trailer rather than reproduced here.

spatial.oracle: the sequence completes. NOTHING WE HAVE CATCHES THIS, and measuring that is the row's purpose. The crossing is between two members of ONE allocation, so every per-allocation bound -- shrink, sublet, the pool arms, CHERI -- is in bounds for it. The authority that would have to be narrowed is per struct member, which means the compiler or the allocation site, not an allocator. That is the taxonomy's partial-squared cell, where table6-cheri-vs-capstone-explained.md already gives CHERI and Capstone the same verdict.
spatial.note: Measured as probe case 41 of ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/security-tests (pool-lifetime-probes.c), which is how pool-repros measures its own Capstone arms. The probe ASSERTS the crossing happened -- the neighbouring member's sentinel must change and its far end must survive -- so a completion is a measurement and not a quiet nothing. verify-outcomes.py's fault predicate deliberately does not list these cases, because a crossing inside one allocation is in bounds for every per-allocation bound.

native-detect.oracle: NO ASan report, MEASURED two-sided. The member-to-member crossing is inside one allocation, so there is no redzone to poison; a write one uint16_t PAST the same allocation is the positive control and ASan does report it (heap-buffer-overflow, exit 1). Without that control the silence would say nothing about the subject and something about the instrument -- and the first build of the probe proved the point: at -O1 the control was silent too, because the dead store had been optimised away.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm's write crosses into the neighbouring member and the sentinel there changes; the fixed arm's bound keeps every write inside its own member. This pair differs by the upstream fix, not by protection -- which is the ONLY oracle available for this class.

backing.oracle: not applicable, and recorded rather than omitted: there is no backing allocation distinct from the object. The object IS one av_malloc (av_refstruct_allocz -> refstruct.c:109, av_malloc(size + REFCOUNT_OFFSET)), so the 'a mechanism at the wrong point' distinction this arm draws for the pool corpus has nothing to separate here.
